title: Zone vs. gap blocking: two ways to block a run (and how to spot each in your drill)
html:
Why this lesson now: the Film Room mirror (football-brief, branch film-room) was checked this run. It still holds one logged game file (data/games/gmum7mktl1wy3.json, "Eagles at Bears, Week 3", no snaps logged) and no review files. The original football-film-room repository wasn't reachable (access denied: "not configured for this session"). So there's no new miss of yours to fix, and no snap of yours this connects to yet. This lesson adds a new idea from Saturday: three teams won with big runs (Oregon's Dierre Hill Jr., Penn State's Carson Hansen, Tennessee's 240 rushing yards).

The big idea: every run play has a blocking plan. There are two main families.Zone: the linemen block an area, not a man. Gap (also called power): the linemen block specific men, and one lineman runs across to lead the way.Lesson 14 showed the gaps from the defense's side. This lesson is the offense's side.

Top: A = zone, all five linemen step right together. Bottom: B = the linemen on the right block down toward the middle. C = the left guard pulls behind them. D = the hole the RB runs through, right behind the guard.

  1. A · Zone. At the snap, all five linemen step the same way, side by side.Each blocks whoever shows up in his area. The RB aims outside and watches the blocks. If a hole opens inside, he cuts back (the dashed line).The RB picks the hole. That's why zone backs need patience and vision.
  2. B · Block down. In a gap play, the linemen on the play side block toward the middle, at an angle.That opens a space just outside them.
  3. C · The pull. A guard from the other side runs behind the line and kicks out (or leads through on) the first defender in that space.It gives the play one extra blocker exactly where the ball is going.
  4. D · The hole. The coach picked this hole before the snap. The RB follows the guard through it.Gap plays hit faster and harder, but if one block fails, there's no other hole to choose.
  5. Which teams use which? Kyle Shanahan's 49ers are the classic NFL zone team: the whole line moves sideways at the snap.Most teams use both. Watch the guards on the replay: if one pulls across, it's a gap play.Saturday's long runs (Hill's 48-yard TD, Hansen's 36-yard run to ice the Penn State game) are good ones to rewatch. Look at the guards first. The box score can't tell you which scheme it was.
  6. Why it matters for bets: zone runs break long when a defense over-pursues sideways. Gap runs grind out short yards and run the clock.A team that can win with gap runs late (like Penn State's last drive) can protect a lead and keep a total low (Lesson 31).

In your drill: you call run or pass before the snap. Blocking happens after. But you can grade yourself after each run: write "Z" if the line stepped together, "G" if a guard pulled.

Two pre-snap hints for a gap run: an extra tight end or fullback next to the line (Lesson 1), and a heavy box (Lesson 19). Zone teams often run from shotgun with the RB beside the QB.

Real examples to watch (Pacific time): today, Texans at Chargers (1:05 p.m., CBS): Woody Marks is Houston's lead back with David Montgomery out. Count his zone cutbacks. Tonight, Buccaneers at Bears (5:20 p.m., NBC): Bucky Irving (5.0 yards a carry). Watch for a pulling guard on short-yardage runs.

Video: search YouTube for "outside zone vs power run explained," "pulling guard counter play," and "Shanahan outside zone breakdown."

Practice it in Football Camp → (Station 5: Plays)

quiz.q: At the snap, all five linemen step to the right together. What kind of run is it?
quiz.w: Zone: the line blocks areas, moving side by side. The RB then picks the hole.

quiz.q: In a gap play, what does the pulling guard do?
o: Blocks the man in front of him
Runs behind the line to the play side and blocks there
quiz.w: He leaves his spot and leads the way, giving one extra blocker at the hole (C in the diagram).

quiz.q: Who chooses the hole on a zone run?
o: The running back, by reading the blocks
quiz.w: On zone, the RB aims outside and cuts back if a hole opens inside. On gap runs, the hole is set before the snap.

quiz.q: You're rewatching a run and want to know if it was gap or zone. What do you look at first?
o: The guards: did one pull across?
quiz.w: A pulling guard is the clearest sign of a gap play. If the whole line moves sideways together, it's zone.
